record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are provided, but the code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a harmful-minus-harmless difference vector and a behavioral effect from steering against it, but uses a single-layer negative steering intervention rather than the original all-layer, all-position projection. It is a conceptual test, not an explicit reproduction.
record.gate_note: The README reports behavioral outcomes for baseline and vector-ablation conditions. The prompt counts and vector-extraction recipe describe the setup, not separate outcome rows. The PCA is described as showing linear separability, but no quantitative PCA result is given.
record.test_reason: The README computes a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference vector at Layer 15 of Llama-3-8B-Instruct (4-bit). It subtracts the normalized vector at that layer (α=2.5) and reports refusal on harmful prompts dropping from ~100% to ~0-25%. That bears on V1's removal claim. The method differs from the original: single-layer additive steering rather than directional projection at every layer and position.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude refusal is encoded as a linearly separable direction, and that subtracting it at Layer 15 bypasses guardrails ('single-vector ablation defeats' safety training). They call this brittleness. They caveat that polysemantic entanglement may cause unintended side effects, and propose SAEs as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The README computes a harmful-minus-harmless mean activation difference, but subtracts a normalized vector at Layer 15 with a tuned strength rather than projecting it out at every layer and position. This is a GitHub research repo; its scripts were not inspected or run.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported intervention is at Layer 15 and uses α=2.5; no comparison across layers or strengths is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: A PCA of Layer 15 activations is said to show harmful and harmless prompts as linearly separable clusters. This is qualitative only, with no numbers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful and harmless prompts are linearly separable in mid-layer activations.

record.problems: The README gives broad approximate ranges for refusal rate and ASR without uncertainty estimates. No capability-retention result is reported. The code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No additional behavioral results stated in the README were left out.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; ablation at all layers and positions; whether other capabilities are retained (the README only speculates about side effects).
Whether real jailbreaks act by suppressing the direction, and whether training against ablation adds robustness. The study's 'ASR' is just its own steering intervention.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal GitHub README, not peer reviewed, and the code was not inspected. The prompt sets are small (N=80), and the same prompts may have been used both to extract the vector and to evaluate it. How refusal and ASR were judged is not stated, and results are reported only as rough ranges. V3 links were removed because 'ASR' measures the authors' own steering, not jailbreak mechanisms.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests, removal at every layer and position, or whether other abilities remain intact.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
Tests a negative-vector intervention as an attack, but not whether naturally occurring attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
Does not distinguish harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.

rows.subject: mlx-community/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-4bit
rows.operation_detail: Subtract the normalized harmful-minus-harmless vector from Layer 15 activations with α=2.5; the README calls this vector ablation
rows.note: The reported intervention subtracts the vector at one layer; it is not described as projecting the direction out at every layer and position.
rows.check: The range ~0-25% includes full removal, and at worst a large majority of refusals are removed. That is not clearly incomplete, so the state is observed rather than partial. The value is an approximate range with no uncertainty, and the refusal-judging method is unstated.

rows.subject: mlx-community/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-4bit
rows.note: Baseline ASR for the harmful-prompt benchmark.
rows.check: ASR here is the complement of R1's refusal rate under the same condition. It is not a natural jailbreak, so it bears on V1 (removal), not V3. The row is redundant with R1. As a baseline control, 0% ASR is just the reference value.

rows.subject: mlx-community/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-4bit
rows.operation_detail: Subtract the normalized harmful-minus-harmless vector from Layer 15 activations with α=2.5; the README calls this vector ablation
rows.note: The README defines ASR as the percentage of harmful prompts that bypass safety guardrails under the intervention.
rows.check: This is the same intervention and outcome as R2, re-expressed as ASR (75-100%). The steering is the authors' own activation edit, not a jailbreak whose mechanism is analysed, so it does not test V3. It duplicates R2.

relationships.condition: Llama-3-8B-Instruct 4-bit, 80 harmful prompts, subtraction at Layer 15 only, α=2.5
relationships.reason: Refusal falls from ~100% (R1) to ~0-25% (R2), equivalently ASR 0% to 75-100% (R3, R4). The figures are approximate ranges with no uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: Refusal fell from approximately 100% to 0–25%, corresponding to an attack-success increase from 0% to approximately 75–100%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
